Answer: A
Reason: The chest radiograph demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear to have central lucency or cavitation (particularly in the right mid-lung and left upper zone), which is the hallmark radiographic presentation of septic pulmonary emboli. This distinguishes it from simple effusions, edema, or non-cavitating metastases.
